label: Formulated and introduced Sunyata (Emptiness & Dependent Arising)
Formulated the Two Truths doctrine (conventional vs. ultimate truth) to resolve the apparent paradox between emptiness and empirical causality
Śaṅkara adopted Nāgārjuna's negative dialectical method while rejecting Śūnyatā as crypto-nihilism, positing immutable Brahman as the transcendent witness behind illusion (Māyā)
Nāgārjuna's deconstruction of intrinsic essence (svabhāva) anticipated Derrida's deconstruction of the metaphysics of presence and origin
Parallel therapeutic methods: Nāgārjuna used dialectic to dissolve metaphysical dogmas just as Wittgenstein sought to dissolve language-bewitchment
Schopenhauer explicitly acknowledged Madhyamaka and Buddhist emptiness as the historical counterpart to his metaphysics of the denial of the Will
